entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv7000"/><div sID="gen10743" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv7000"/>2. Deference, submission, and trust, are all expressed by the figure. In the East, servants in attending on their masters are almost wholly directed by signs, which require the closest observance of the hands of the latter. The servants of God should look (1) to His directing hand, to appoint them their work; (2) to His supplying hand (<reference osisRef="Ps.104.28">Psa 104:28</reference>), to give them their portion in due season; (3) to His protecting hand, to right them when wronged; (4) to His correcting hand (<reference osisRef="Isa.9.13">Is 9:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Pet.5.6">1Pe 5:6</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Gen.16.6">Ge 16:6</reference>); (<reference osisRef="Gen.16.5">5</reference>) to His rewarding hand. <div eID="gen10743" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 2. Deference, submission, and trust, are all expressed by the figure.
